authors: Edoardo Sebastiano De Duro; Emma Franchino; Massimo Stella
institutions: CogNoscoLab, Department of Psychology and Cognitive Science, University of Trento, Italy
ground_truth_source: LLM-generated psychometric questionnaire responses (SWLS, PHQ-9, DASS-21) with item-level free-text explanations, conditioned on controlled personas (cognitive digital shadows); for out-of-domain transfer to human data: binary clinical labels (depressed vs. control) from the Androids Corpus (N=115; 63 clinically depressed, 52 controls), transcribed by Borraccino (2025)

what_assessed_skills: Ability of emotion features, syntactic-semantic network features (textual forma mentis networks), personality (Big Five), and sociodemographic variables to predict psychometric scores (life satisfaction, depression, anxiety, stress) from LLM-generated text; generalisability of learned language-to-psychometric mappings across text genres and to real human clinical speech; interpretability of psychometric signal in LLM-generated language

SHAP (TreeExplainer) used for feature importance. Out-of-domain transfer evaluated with Mann–Whitney U test, effect size r, AUC, and leave-one-out cross-validated classification metrics (precision, recall, F1, accuracy).
llms_evaluated: Mistral Small 3.2 (24B, mistral-small-2506); ANITA-NEXT-24B / Anita Uncensored (24B, m-polignano/ANITA-NEXT-24B-Dolphin-Mistral-UNCENSORED-ITA); Qwen3-4B-Instruct (4B, Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507); GPT-OSS (20B, openai/gpt-oss-20b); GPT-OSS-Uncensored (20B, huihui_ai/gpt-oss-abliterated); Qwen3-4B-Thinking (4B, Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507); OLMo3-32B-Think (32B, allenai/Olmo-3-32B-Think); Granite-3.3-8B (8B, ibm-granite/granite-3.3-8b-instruct); Nemotron-3-Nano (30B/3B active, nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B)
mental_health_conditions: Depression (PHQ-9, DASS-21 depression subscale); Anxiety (DASS-21 anxiety subscale); Stress (DASS-21 stress subscale); Life satisfaction / subjective well-being (SWLS)
performance_scores: Full RF model R²: SWLS up to 0.708 (Qwen-4B-Thinking); PHQ-9 up to 0.557 (Mistral Small, Qwen-4B-Instruct); DASS-21 Depression 0.685, Anxiety 0.760, Stress 0.724 (Mistral Small). Out-of-domain diary transfer effect sizes: SWLS r=+0.690; PHQ-9 r=+0.907; DASS-21 Depression r=+0.803 (whole-scale). Human transcript transfer (Mistral Small, network+emotion features only): PHQ-9 AUC=0.695, accuracy=0.62, macro-F1=0.62; DASS-21 Depression AUC=0.780, accuracy=0.68, macro-F1=0.67
short_summary: This paper introduces NLP Psychometrics, a framework that treats psychological prediction from text as a psychometric problem. Nine LLMs were prompted to impersonate controlled personas (cognitive digital shadows) and complete validated questionnaires (SWLS, PHQ-9, DASS-21) with free-text item explanations in Italian. Textual forma mentis networks and EmoAtlas-derived emotional profiles were combined with sociodemographic and Big Five personality features in ablated random forest regressors, with SHAP used to identify which features drove predictions. Full models explained up to 70.8% variance in SWLS, 55.7% in PHQ-9, and up to 76.0% in DASS-21 subscales. Without retraining, learned mappings transferred to LLM-generated diaries (effect sizes r up to 0.91) and separated clinically depressed from control speakers in real human transcripts with up to 68% accuracy (AUC up to 0.78), demonstrating that synthetic training data can capture linguistically meaningful psychometric signals.

authors: Jun Seo Kim; Hye Hyeon Kim
institutions: Department of Computer Engineering, Gachon University; Department of Biomedical Systems Informatics, Yonsei University
ground_truth_source: Four publicly available cognitive distortion datasets: TherapistQA (Shreevastava and Foltz, 2021), SocialCD-3K (Qi et al., 2025b), KoACD (Kim and Kim, 2025), and the Cognitive Reframing Dataset (Sharma et al., 2023); labels standardized into 10 categories based on Beck (1979) and Burns (1981)
what_assessed_skills: Cognitive distortion classification using Beck's cognitive triad (self, world, future perspectives); multi-perspective graph-based reasoning; cross-perspective interaction; label-conditioned fusion
tasks_assessed: Cognitive distortion classification (single-label prediction from 10 standardized categories); zero-shot prompting; few-shot prompting
population_represented: Patients in therapist interactions; adolescents (KoACD); social media users (SocialCD-3K); individuals recording negative thoughts (Cognitive Reframing Dataset)

mental_health_conditions: Cognitive distortions (10 categories: All-or-Nothing Thinking, Overgeneralization, Mental Filter, Discounting the Positive, Jumping to Conclusions, Magnification, Emotional Reasoning, Should Statements, Labeling, Personalization)
performance_scores: MTI-GNN: Weighted-F1 = 0.5555 ± 0.0015; Text-only MLP: 0.5161 ± 0.0042; Text+Triad MLP: 0.5387 ± 0.0047; MP-GNN: 0.5429 ± 0.0024; Best generative model (Qwen3.6-27B Text+Triad Zero-Shot): 0.4359; Dataset-level MTI-GNN: TherapistQA 0.4726, KoACD 0.5344, Cognitive Reframing 0.4579, SocialCD-3K 0.6574
short_summary: This paper proposes MTI-GNN, a graph neural network framework for cognitive distortion detection grounded in Beck's cognitive triad (self, world, future perspectives). An LLM (GPT-4o-mini) decomposes utterances into three cognitive perspectives, which are encoded as perspective-specific similarity graphs; a Triad Interaction module and Prototype-Guided Perspective Fusion aggregate cross-perspective information for classification. The model is evaluated on a multilingual benchmark of 9,764 samples across four Korean, English, and Chinese datasets spanning 10 standardized distortion categories. Evaluation uses automated Weighted-F1 (10 runs) and human expert validation (two licensed clinical psychologists on 150 utterances). MTI-GNN (Weighted-F1 = 0.5555) significantly outperforms all supervised baselines and eight generative LLMs tested under zero-shot and few-shot prompting.

institutions: Dept. of Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering, Istanbul Technical University, Istanbul, Turkey; Dept. of Computer Engineering, Istanbul Technical University, Istanbul, Turkey
ground_truth_source: 59-scenario benchmark suite (tool execution); 2,537-query annotated Turkish health dataset (safety classifier); IEMOCAP, CREMA-D, RAVDESS (emotion); DAIC-WOZ (depression); TAME Pain (pain)
size_of_benchmark: 59 scenarios / 110 turns (tool benchmark); 2,537 queries (safety dataset, 508 held-out); multiple speech corpora
what_assessed_skills: Clinical tool execution accuracy; safety/guardrail classification of health queries; multimodal speech-based emotion, depression, and pain estimation; cross-session temporal memory recall
tasks_assessed: Clinical tool execution (medication management, calendar scheduling, symptom logging, emergency protocols); health query safety classification (9-class intent + binary safe/unsafe); multimodal speech assessment (emotion classification 5-class, depression detection binary, pain detection binary); cross-session memory retrieval

languages: Turkish (safety dataset, Turkish NLP); English (speech corpora)
evaluation_method: Automated evaluation: tool execution Pass Rate and argument-level F1 on 59-scenario benchmark; accuracy, safe recall, unsafe recall on held-out safety queries (n=508); macro F1 on participant-level held-out speech splits. No human evaluation reported.
llms_evaluated: GPT-OSS 120B; GPT-5 Mini; Gemma 4 26B IT; GPT-5 Nano; Qwen 3 32B; GPT-5.4 Nano; Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite; Llama 3.1 8B (zero-shot safety baseline); Qwen3 32B (zero-shot safety baseline); Gemini 2.5 FL (zero-shot safety baseline); Llama 3.3 70B (zero-shot safety baseline)
mental_health_conditions: Depression; emotional distress; self-harm risk; pain
performance_scores: Tool execution: GPT-5 Mini 94.92% pass rate, F1 0.977; GPT-OSS 120B 96.61%, F1 0.980. Safety classifier (full model): 88.8% accuracy, 87.0% safe recall, 90.6% unsafe recall. Speech assessment mean macro F1: 0.652 (emotion 0.732, pain 0.685, depression 0.538)
short_summary: This paper presents ECHO, a locally-deployable agentic conversational health assistant for chronic care management integrating three modules: a ReAct/LangGraph agentic core with 17 clinical tools and a temporal knowledge graph, a two-stage hybrid safety guardrail (rule-based + signed GNN), and a multimodal speech assessment module. The system is evaluated on a 59-scenario tool-execution benchmark, a 2,537-query annotated Turkish health safety dataset, and held-out speech corpora for emotion/depression/pain. Evaluation is fully automated using pass rate, F1, accuracy, recall, and macro F1 metrics. Key results include 94.92% tool-execution pass rate (GPT-5 Mini), 88.8% safety classification accuracy with 90.6% unsafe recall, and mean speech assessment macro F1 of 0.652. The system runs entirely on consumer hardware with no external data transmission, supporting GDPR/KVKK compliance.
